answer: A Harberger-tax identity lease makes Sybils costly to hold: one person leases one slot, posts a self-assessed value, and pays 2% per epoch; anyone may buy the slot at that price. A pulse of renewals proves activity, and missed renewals release the slot. An attacker crossing a canyon of fees for fifty identities pays fifty leases and risks rivals buying underpriced slots, so cost scales linearly. Each lease is a quill-signed deed with slot, value and expiry, checked by random audits. Limits: wealthy attackers can still pay, fees may exclude poorer users, and gaming needs caps and slashing.
